standing_constraints: ACCEPTANCE TESTS FOR THIS FEATURE ARE OFF LIMITS. No step may create, edit or delete any file under tests/acceptance/cluster-board-control/. They are DISTILL's authored specification and they are what 'done' means. If a scenario looks wrong, STOP and escalate — never edit an assertion to meet the behaviour.

TWO test files outside that directory ARE in scope and are named explicitly in the steps that touch them: tests/acceptance/sqlite-backend/test_repository_contract.py (lines 97-100 only — authorised by ADR-009 DDD-6) and tests/unit/test_live_board_off_switch.py (the shipped unit tests, which assert the representation being replaced).

DO NOT AMEND MIGRATION 0005 AFTER THIS BRANCH IS PUSHED. Amending in place is legitimate ONLY because no database has ever run it (ADR-009 DDD-4, verified: branch is 8 commits ahead of main and unpushed). If that stops being true, stop and chain a 0006 instead.

KPI-1 and KPI-2 in docs/product/kpi-contracts.yaml name two tests in tests/unit/test_live_board_off_switch.py as their measuring assertions (test_a_board_that_is_off_is_left_completely_alone, test_the_switch_survives_the_sqlite_round_trip). Those two tests must SURVIVE the refactor, adapted to the new representation. Deleting either one silently dangles a HARD KPI gate.
Never push to any branch and never open a PR. The operator merges via PR; DELIVER commits locally only.

build_order_constraint: 01-01 before 01-02 is a hard ordering: 01-02's adapters read the column 01-01 creates. 01-02 CANNOT be decomposed further — changing load_live_leaderboards' return type breaks all ten call sites in the same instant, so the type, both adapters and every call site land together or the suite is red at COMMIT. A shim in bot/guilds.py that converted back to dicts was considered and rejected: it is the fallback-coexistence the Wave Completion Enforcement rule forbids, and it would be deleted in the very next step. 02-01 is independent and additive and could run before or after Phase 01; it runs after because it is easier to assert a state change once the state has one representation.

phases.name: Conform the representation
phases.description: US-004, the @infrastructure precursor. Replace the shipped boolean-omitted-when-true convention with the enum-valued status and frozen dataclass the codebase already uses for a guild key.

steps.name: Amend 0005 and rename the stored column
criteria: Migration 0005 adds board_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' in place of enabled BOOLEAN
LiveLeaderboardRow.board_status replaces enabled; downgrade still uses native op.drop_column, not batch mode
Upgrading a database that already holds configured boards leaves every board reading active
The port still returns and accepts the shipped dict shape, so no call site changes in this step
Full suite still 52 failed / 358 passed; lint-imports still 0 broken
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-009 DDD-1 and DDD-4. This step changes STORAGE ONLY and deliberately leaves the port speaking the old dict shape — that is what keeps the suite at its baseline while the column moves. The adapter translates internally: load emits entry['enabled'] = False when row.board_status == 'disabled'; save writes row.board_status = 'disabled' if entry.get('enabled', True) is False else 'active'. That translation is temporary scaffolding for exactly one step and 01-02 deletes it. KEEP THE EXISTING DOCSTRING FINDING about native DROP COLUMN vs batch_alter_table — it holds regardless of column type, it was learned the hard way, and test_downgrade_restores_the_prior_shape_exactly (guild-key-integrity) compares stored DDL as text. Verified safe: that test's db_at_previous_head fixture pins PRE_FEATURE_HEAD absolutely, not as a distance from head, so amending 0005 cannot move it. Store the literal string values, not the enum — policy depends on storage, never the reverse (ADR-008 D3), which is why KeyStatus's values are duplicated at the storage layer rather than imported. The module filename 0005_live_leaderboard_enabled.py now misdescribes itself; grep for the basename first and if genuinely nothing references it, rename to 0005_live_leaderboard_board_status.py. Alembic keys off the `revision` string, not the filename, so this is safe — but verify before doing it, and skip the rename rather than guess.

steps.name: Move LiveBoardConfig across the port
criteria: LiveBoardConfig.is_enabled returns the status comparison and the __SCAFFOLD__ marker is gone
Both adapters return dict[str, LiveBoardConfig] and materialise ACTIVE when no status is stored
All ten call sites pass and receive configs; live_board_enabled and set_live_board_enabled are deleted
The refresh loop rebuilds configs with dataclasses.replace instead of mutating them in place
Only bot/repository.py compares a status literal anywhere in production
steps.sizing_review: @sizing-review-needed — 19 scenarios, above the 8 threshold. Reviewed and ACCEPTED as irreducible on 2026-09-08. The threshold exists to catch a step doing several unrelated things; this step does ONE thing (change a port's return type) whose blast radius is 19 scenarios wide because ten call sites read that port. Splitting it leaves the suite red at an intermediate COMMIT, which Mandate 7 forbids. THE MAJORITY OF THESE SCENARIOS REQUIRE NO NEW BEHAVIOUR: the two commands, the refusal paths, the tier check, the /view_config status line and the rollover handling all shipped in f20227a and work today. They are failing only because the suite's port guard rejects the dict-shaped port. They are named here as REGRESSION EVIDENCE for DESIGN's load-bearing claim — 'the whole DESIGN wave is behaviour-preserving at every driving port' — which is a claim about tests that must go green without their assertions changing. TestBoardStatusJourney is listed for the same reason and needs no implementation of its own: it is the property-based counterpart to test_a_board_that_is_off_is_never_touched_by_the_cycle, proving KPI-1 across generated interleavings rather than one. It is NOT given its own step because a step with an empty files_to_modify is a validation-only step, which the orchestrator's automated gate rejects.

My implementation_notes asserted that every test touching /set_live_leaderboard 'uses a repository DOUBLE, so those tests stay green while production breaks'. That was half right and the wrong half mattered: the double stores what the command saved, and this test's own _surface helper then reads a field off the stored object — `board.get("season")` at line 294, which is a dict call on what is now a frozen dataclass. steps.implementation_notes: ADR-009 DDD-2, DDD-3, DDD-6, DDD-7, DDD-8. THE ATOMIC STEP — see build_order_constraint for why it cannot be split. MEASURED CALL SITES (grepped 2026-09-08, not estimated; the DESIGN figure of '4 reads and 2 writes' was wrong and hid a whole driving port — UI-4): load_live_leaderboards at admin_cog 437/589/713/776 and tasks_cog 556; save_live_leaderboards at admin_cog 596/723/799, tasks_cog 723 and migrations_json_to_sqlite 511. THE ONE THAT BITES: admin_cog 589-596 is /set_live_leaderboard, the GUILD-scoped setup command, which writes a raw dict literal into the mapping. Every existing test that touches it uses a repository DOUBLE, so those tests stay green while production breaks — which is precisely why test_setting_up_a_guild_board_still_stores_something_readable was added against both real adapters. admin_cog 713-723 is the cluster setup command and must keep re-enabling on setup (AC-002.5): building a fresh LiveBoardConfig gives that for free, since board_status defaults to ACTIVE. JSON ON-DISK SHAPE: keep it a plain dict (brief.md section C says the JSON file shape stays accurate as the on-disk form) and always write board_status; a file written before the column existed simply has no key and load materialises ACTIVE, which is DDD-3. Do NOT reintroduce omit-when-default in either adapter — that convention is the defect this step removes. tasks_cog: config['messages'] = ... and config['season'] = ... at 669 and 712-713 mutate a frozen dataclass and will raise; rebuild with dataclasses.replace and write the result back into the live mapping. DESIGN open question Q4 is yours to answer: decide whether the `dirty` flag is still the right mechanism once the mapping is rebuilt, and record the answer. Q2 is also yours: BoardStatus currently sits in bot/repository.py and STATUS_COMPARISON_OWNER in the test vocabulary pins it there — moving it means the acceptance test fails, so leave it unless you have a strong reason and escalate if you do. TEST EDITS AUTHORISED HERE, AND ONLY THESE: test_repository_contract.py 97-100, where the exact-equality literal must carry a LiveBoardConfig (DDD-6 — the contract genuinely changed, and amending the test to match an intended change is a different act from bending production to avoid amending it, which is what produced the shipped shape); and tests/unit/test_live_board_off_switch.py, whose test_enabling_never_writes_a_true_flag asserts the convention being deleted and should go, while test_a_config_with_no_flag_is_on keeps its claim (AC-004.3) and changes its mechanism. KPI-1 and KPI-2 name two tests in that file — see standing_constraints; both must survive.

phases.name: The operator's record
phases.description: US-005. The one genuinely new behaviour in this wave: a paused board leaves a trace an operator can find months later, when nobody remembers pausing it.

steps.name: Record a board's state change
criteria: A real state change emits exactly one live_board.status.changed record
The record names the scope key and both the previous and the new status
A no-op flip emits no record at all
The hourly cycle emits no record for a paused board, however many times it runs
steps.implementation_notes: US-005, and OD-1 in kpi-contracts.yaml. USE bot/obs.py emit_structured — do not write a second structured-log helper. Two divergent JSON log schemas is exactly what that module exists to prevent, and every KPI query in kpi-contracts.yaml assumes one shape. Pass the emitting module's own logger, not a shared one, so the record lands under bot.cogs.admin_cog and the operator can tell where it came from. The event name is live_board.status.changed and it is pinned in the test vocabulary as BOARD_STATUS_CHANGED_EVENT — the operator's grep and the test have to break together, so do not rename it. emit_structured attaches fields via extra=, which is how the board_events fixture asserts on record.event without re-parsing JSON; that is already handled by the helper. PLACEMENT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN: the record follows the CHANGE, not the command. Emit it after the save, past the no-op early return — if it sits at the top of the handler the log answers 'who ran a command' rather than 'when did the state move', and AC-005.2 fails. Nothing is emitted from the refresh loop: ~720 records a month for one paused board is how a log stops being read (AC-005.3). The existing print() in the refresh loop skip branch is NOT the record and must not be promoted into one — leave it or drop it, but do not make the hourly cycle emit a structured event.
